'''George Bernard Benedek''' (December 1, 1928 – July 5, 2026) was an American physicist and the [[Alfred H. Caspary]] Professor Emeritus of Physics and Biological Physics and of Health Sciences and Technology at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hst.mit.edu/faculty-research/faculty/benedek-george|title=George Bernard Benedek, PhD|date=January 23, 2020|publisher=Harvart MIT Health Sciences and Technology|accessdate= June 30, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://imes.mit.edu/people/faculty/benedek-george-b/ |title=George B. Benedek |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=May 1, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170422134811/http://imes.mit.edu/people/faculty/benedek-george-b/ |archive-date=April 22, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://web.mit.edu/physics/people/faculty/benedek_george.html |title=George Benedek |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=May 1, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://web.mit.edu/physics/benedek/ |title=George Benedek |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=May 1, 2017}}</ref>

Benedek graduated BS in physics at [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in 1949, AM in physics at [[Harvard University]] in 1952 and PhD in physics from Harvard University in 1953; he was a doctoral student of [[Edward Mills Purcell]].<ref name=":0" />

Benedek died in [[Winchester, Massachusetts]], on July 5, 2026, at the age of 97.<ref>{{cite web |title=George B. Benedek |url=https://brezniakfuneraldirectors.com/obituary-archive/george-b-benedek/ |website=Brezniak Funeral Directors |access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> He was the father of [[Emily Benedek]].

==Awards and honors==
Benedek invented [[Dynamic_light_scattering|quasi-elastic light scattering]] spectroscopy and in 1962 was made a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]].

*American Physical Society Fellow (1962)
*National Academy of Sciences Member (1981)
*American Academy of Arts and Sciences Member (1988)
*Irving Langmuir Prize in Chemical Physics (APS) (1995) "For his outstanding invention of dynamic light scattering spectroscopy and its fundamental applications to critical phenomena, macromolecular transport, and ocular diseases."
*The Vinci of Excellence "Science for Art" Prize (1995)
*Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology's (ARVO) Proctor Medal (1997) for "outstanding research in basic or clinical sciences as applied to ophthalmology"<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://physics.mit.edu/faculty/george-benedek/ |title=George Benedek |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref>
